articles.title: Sunderland 0-2 Dinamo Zagreb: Regis Le Bris under more pressure as Black Cats beaten in the Europa League
articles.summary: Match report as Sunderland were beaten 2-0 by Dinamo Zagreb to take the Black Cats' run to one win in six in all competitions; Luka Stojkovic volleyed in the first for the Croatian side before setting up Dion Beljo for a second before half-time; Regis Le Bris is firmly under pressure
articles.body:
Before the game, Le Bris said Sunderland have been too exposed and leaky in defence - but his team were not listening as they went in 2-0 down at half-time in front of an angry Stadium of Light.

Poor marking from a corner allowed Luka Stojkovic to volley in the first goal - then the Dinamo midfielder set up Dion Beljo with a delightful chipped pass, with his deft finish equally sweet, although the red and white defenders were all at sea in the move.

At the other end of the pitch, Sunderland were a little more unfortunate. They struck the woodwork in both halves through defenders Thomas Meunier and Kevin Danso. Heroic defending from Dinamo also denied Malick Fofana and Trai Hume in the same move with last-ditch blocks.

Not even a quadruple half-time substitution by head coach Le Bris and the introduction of Brian Brobbey later in the second half could inspire a comeback.

But for Le Bris, he is now facing a run of just one win across six games in all competitions. Bottom of the Premier League, now Sunderland's league form is drifting into Europe.

With Sunderland booed off at half and full-time, and fans rushing for the exits long before the full-time whistle, how much credit in the bank does the Frenchman still have?

Key moments from the Stadium of Light...

10: CHANCE! Chris Rigg crosses for Jules Ahoka whose header is straight at the Dinamo goalkeeper.

22: BIG BLOCK! Beljo has a clear sight of goal for Dinamo but Granit Xhaka comes across with a last-dtich block.

23: GOAL! The resulting corner sees Stojkovic given space to crack a shot at goal and he obliges with a stunning volley.

24: OFF THE LINE! Dinamo nearly make it 2-0 but Meunier denies Milan Orsic with a goal-line clearance.

30: OFF THE POST! Meunier's cross is so deep it comes off the woodwork, nearly catching the goalkeeper out.

40: GOAL ! Stojkovic's clipped pass finds Beljo in space and he finishes to make it 2-0.

47: GOAL DISALLOWED! Xhaka crosses for Wilson Isidor to head home from close range - but it is ruled out for offside by VAR.

58: OFF THE BAR! Following wave after wave of Sunderland attacks, Reinildo's header is clawed out by the goalkeeper, then Danso strikes the bar with a hooked finish on the rebound.

67: CHANCE! Brobbey comes on and nearly gets a goal back, but he is denied by the goalkeeper from close range after Xhaka's smart pass.

Le Bris: The most important game is Chelsea this Sunday

Sunderland head coach Regis Le Bris to TNT Sports:

"Tough period. We had two different halves. The first one was difficult with many young players. This period is not easy to manage and we felt even if they tried, it's heavy at the minute. It's not easy to change the dynamic.

"I appreciated the reaction in the second half, even though there were more experienced players. More quality, more experience on the pitch. We are unlucky because we created many chances but it wasn't enough. It's like this, when you go on a poor run it's hard to change the dynamic.

"We are still combative, the players tried until the end to show something different. We know that the most important game this week is at the end of the week against Chelsea.

"I'm pleased with the energy, competitiveness until the end. Now we need more quality, it's fair to say that, because at the minute it's not the case."

Are Sunderland out of confidence? "Probably. We have good players, a good team. I believe this team has a really big potential. We showed it last season. But you also have to experience tough situations. Last season, it happened a bit later when we had 30, 35 points.

"Now the situation is different. This situation will define us as well as a team, as a club, with our fans, with staff - we'll stick together and be combative until the end."

Underprepared and underwhelming, Sunderland are sliding away

Just where has last season's Sunderland gone? The team that was tough to beat, capable of finding solutions and demonstrating resilience has disappeared this season.

What Sunderland are going through right now is what many expected them to be like last season. Except this year, they are not a newly-promoted side, they are a team in Europe.

Ultimately, the Thursday-Sunday schedule is taking its toll and this result has proven that Sunderland's depth is not good enough. The likes of Jules Ahoka, Thomas Meunier and Chris Rigg were all taken off at half-time. And that does not bode well with the fixture schedule only piling further and further up.

Le Bris ultimately chose Chelsea as the priority match this week. His six changes for this game spoke volumes about how they cannot handle their European commitments with this level of squad, with this lack of confidence.

Sunderland need the international break, then they need the January window. Le Bris right now looks the victim of his own success, but is it getting to a point where he is becoming the villain of his own hero story?

articles.title: Cal GM Ron Rivera Drops Honest Quote on HC Tosh Lupoi Amid 3-6 Record in 1st Season
articles.summary: As Cal struggles through a 3-6 season, general manager Ron Rivera isn't mincing words when it comes to first-year head coach Tosh Lupoi.
articles.body:
As Cal struggles through a 3-6 season, general manager Ron Rivera isn't mincing words when it comes to first-year head coach Tosh Lupoi.

"He has bumped his head a lot. We have talked a lot, tried to give him a lot of advice, point him in the right direction. Some of it, he's been very receptive, and other portions of it, he hasn't," Rivera said during an appearance on KNBR's " Murph & Markus " morning show (h/t Alex Simon of SFGate.com). "And it's those things that sometimes you've gotta learn for yourself before you think, ' Oh wow, this is it.' But I'd like to continue to stress that this is a guy that's learning, growing. But now it's time. These last three games, hopefully four, the trajectory has to be going north. We have to show that we are growing, there has been some growth and development of our players, our team, and the culture is getting stronger. Those are all things that you have to have going forward."

Lupoi, 45, played for Cal as a defensive lineman (2000-05) and also served as a defensive line coach with the team between the 2008-11 seasons. He's also had stops at Washington (2012-13, defensive line coach), Alabama (2014-18), the Cleveland Browns (2019 defensive line), Atlanta Falcons (2020, defensive line and run-game coordinator), the Jacksonville Jaguars (2021, defensive line) and Oregon (2022-25, defensive coordinator and linebackers). He held a number of roles at Alabama, including as the defensive coordinator for two seasons.

Rivera, 64, was hired as the football program's general manager in March 2025. The former Cal and NFL linebacker is best known for his stints as the head coach of the Carolina Panthers (2011-19) and Washington Commanders (2020-23), posting a 102-103-2 record during his NFL coaching career.

Lupoi replaced Justin Wilcox, who posted just three winning seasons in nine years at the helm along with a 1-4 bowl record. Expectations were high coming into the 2026 season, especially as Cal continue to adjust to life in the ACC, but thus far the results haven't followed.

"We've got to get this foundation put down, we've got to show that we have solid roots in the ground, we are ready to go forward," Rivera noted. "Then we can hit the recruiting trail being able to point to the direction, saying, 'Look, we're heading north. We're doing the things that we need to do. We're putting the players in position, so let's roll.' And that's what we have to do."

articles.title: FPL gameweek 10 tips: Should you keep or sell Ezri Konsa?
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Fantasy Premier League expert FPL Heisenberg gives his answers to some of the biggest dilemmas facing managers in gameweek 10.
articles.body:
BBC Sport's Fantasy Premier League expert FPL Heisenberg gives his answers to some of the biggest dilemmas facing managers heading into gameweek 10.

Despite performing so well in recent weeks - helping Arsenal to three clean sheets in three Premier League games - for me defender Ezri Konsa (£4.8m) is not a buy this week.

After the midweek Champions League game, Mikel Arteta mentioned him having some knee problems, which led to his early substitution.

William Saliba is now fit and was even in the squad, so anyone bringing Konsa in now is looking at a sell as early as gameweek 11.

However, for owners he is not an automatic sell either.

There is still a chance he starts Hull at home. I am hoping he either starts or he isn't in the squad.

As an owner I am hoping he is fit enough to start, and then in gameweek 11 or 12 I will look to move him on to a defender with strong defensive-contribution potential - someone like Brighton 's Luka Vuskovic (£5.2m), Liverpool 's Jeremy Jacquet (£5.1m) or Leeds ' Tarik Muharemovic (£5.1m).

Underperforming midfielders - Gibbs-White, Mbeumo, Schade: buy, sell or hold?

We are in a period of the game where defenders look very strong - they offer goal threat, defensive contributions and play for sides with real defensive strength. The days of starting five midfielders feel in the past for now. The meta is closer to four defenders, three or four midfielders, and two or three strikers. Things can shift quickly in FPL, but that is the landscape right now.

If you have midfielders you are not happy with, the answer may not always be to sell them. It can be to bench them some weeks and only play them in the better fixtures.

In isolation, Nottingham Forest 's Morgan Gibbs-White (£7.8m) is still a reasonable pick. He is on penalties, he is the talisman for Forest even when the goals have been scarce, and he plays 90 minutes.

Bryan Mbeumo (£7.9m) is involved in a lot of chances and goals for a Manchester United side that is struggling. He was unlucky not to return against Chelsea .

Kevin Schade (£6.2m) plays for a Brentford team that is on the up and carries attacking threat.

These are decent options. You do not have to force a sale just because they have blanked recently.

There is no clear must-buy in midfield, unless you are without Brighton 's Pascal Gross (£6.2m) or Chelsea 's Morgan Rogers (£8.2m) and you specifically need to move one of these three on. Hold if you can, and reassess if the picture changes.

We are entering a busier stretch where some of the early-season reliable options - Konsa (£4.8m), Brighton 's Maxim de Cuyper (£5.4m) and Arsenal 's Riccardo Calafiori (£5.9m) - may not be as nailed as they have been.

I am not saying sell them all immediately, but it is worth starting to think about how you phase in the next wave of defensive purchases.

Antonio Silva (£5.1m) or James Hill (£5.5m) at Bournemouth both stand out as good options this week and beyond. The underlying defensive data has been solid, and both are excellent for defensive contributions - more than nine per 90 minutes. Playing Ipswich is a decent time to buy.

Muharemovic at Leeds is another. Spurs is not the easiest fixture, but Leeds have been very good at Elland Road, so it is a fair entry point if you want him.

A Liverpool defender is also worth considering. Crystal Palace have struggled and have been vulnerable to set-pieces - Tottenham 's Jan Paul van Hecke had a number of chances and eventually scored last week. Virgil van Dijk (£6.4m) or Jacquet look shrewd buys. If you do not already own De Cuyper, or if you can afford Gabriel (£8.0m), those remain strong options too.

Best picks from Liverpool before a good run?

This is the start of a good run, beginning with Crystal Palace . There are a few options, but each carries some risk. The defenders are the obvious options - Jacquet and Van Dijk both look fine. Midfield is harder.

Bradley Barcola (£8.1m) is getting minutes but the underlying numbers have not been strong. Cody Gakpo (£7.1m) has shown good minutes and data in the past, but the recent early substitutions are a concern while he is competing with Victor Munoz (£6.5m) and Barcola out wide.

Dominik Szoboszlai (£6.7m) has been underwhelming. He is not getting enough game time and his role is unclear. That leaves Alexander Isak (£9.2m).

He is an excellent pick, but at more than £9m he is also expensive. You have to ask why you would take him over Nicolas Jackson (£7.0m), Joao Pedro (£7.7m) and Erling Haaland (£15.8m), or the cheaper options like Thierno Barry (£5.6m) and Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£6.1m). He is good, but he also blocks other good picks. It is perfectly reasonable to wait and look again around gameweek 13, rather than forcing investment now.

Captaincy - Haaland v Gabriel/Calafiori?

Haaland is away at Nottingham Forest . Forest have struggled at both ends, but their attacking and defensive data has actually been reasonable, and Glasner has a history of being difficult to break down against stronger sides from his Palace days. If you want to take on Haaland, this is a reasonable week to do it.

The problem is the alternative options are limited.

The clearest ones are Gabriel or Calafiori. Gabriel brings excellent clean-sheet odds, the chance of a bullet header, and defensive-contribution points. He is probably the strongest rival to Haaland.

In my own team I am looking at Calafiori. He had a full midweek rest so he should start against Hull , and when Arsenal dominate the ball he gets very high up the pitch. Against Hull that could be significant.

We have to start treating defenders as genuine captaincy options given how many double-digit hauls they have produced this season.

My head is still on the safer Haaland pick, but I am very tempted by Calafiori. If you want to go different, an Arsenal defender is the way to go.

articles.title: España-Portugal, semifinal de la 'Finalissima' con sabor a Mundial
articles.standfirst: El partido, repetición de la final de la Eurocopa de Liubliana se podrá ver en el canal de Youtube de la RFEF (22:30)
articles.summary: El partido, repetición de la final de la Eurocopa de Liubliana se podrá ver en el canal de Youtube de la RFEF (22:30)
articles.body: La bella localidad de Niterói, a unos 20 kilómetros de Río de Janeiro, y su Arena, con capacidad para unos 2.500 espectadores en eventos deportivos, acoge la segunda edición de la 'Finalissima' de fútbol sala, o lo que es lo mismo, unas semifinales entre cuatro de los mejores equipos del mundo: España y Portugal, campeón y subcampeón de Europa; y sus homólogos de América: Brasil y Argentina. La organización ha dispuesto que los equipos del mismo continente se vean las caras en semifinales, lo que, de paso, garantiza una final entre un equipo europeo y otro americano (sudamericano, en este caso). España, en esa reconstrucción de su prestigio mundial que va haciendo en cada torneo en el que compite, afronta, tras ganar la Eurocopa, la 'Finalissima' con la máxima ilusión, pero consciente de que Portugal, rival esta noche, le puede ganar: “El torneo reúne muchas motivaciones. Respetamos mucho a Portugal, es un equipo que nos puede hacer daño, nos puede ganar. Somos conscientes de ello. Vamos a ver en qué nivel estamos”, reconoce el seleccionador nacional, Jesús Velasco, que asume que este torneo es: “uno de los más prestigiosos por los equipos que vamos a competir en él”. Será la propia Federación Española, a través de su canal de Youtube, la que retransmita el partidazo que disputan esta noche España y Portugal, repetición de la final de la Eurocopa jugada en Liubliana (3-5) (22:30).
